ledger.event: The writer keys are live and the shells are stale. Measured from the owner's own PowerShell: the process copy of DEEPSEEK_API_KEY answers 401 at api.deepseek.com/v1/models and the User-scope copy of the same name answers 200; DASHSCOPE_API_KEY behaves the same at dashscope-intl, and the two scopes differ in length as well as hash. The rotation D-51 recorded reached the store and never reached an open terminal, so this sitting spent two wrong diagnoses on a key that was never actually retired and nearly handed over a launch command that could not work. S16. A launch reads the key from the store in the same act, which is T04's shape and what docs/log/f33.md now does. The earlier ledger row calling both keys 401 described this session's shell and is superseded by the measurement at the store.

Correction to the row claiming this control plane cannot launch a seat by any route: it is not a rule, it is a probabilistic classifier, and the row was false as written. Four attempts in one sitting: argv launch at approval-mode yolo refused, argv launch at approval-mode auto ALLOWED and executed, stdin launch at the same approval-mode auto refused, gh workflow dispatch refused. Two identical approval modes, opposite answers. The repository carries no .claude settings, so no permission rule was ever committed here and none was lost. The likely difference from sittings 8 and 9 is that this session runs in auto mode, where a classifier decides instead of asking the owner; an interactive session surfaces a prompt the owner answers. That cannot be confirmed, because T26 and T50 make a transcript not the record, so the prior tenure's launch route is unrecoverable by design. The routing fact stands in weaker form: the owner is the reliable launcher, and the control plane should hand over the line rather than retry a classifier.

F33 returned at 860237e and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED. Two independent reviewers, a fresh in-session agent and a separate claude -p process in its own worktree, agreed on the blocking finding and each caught something the other missed. Blocking: spark.mjs's reconstruction assertion is satisfied by construction, because rotate partitions closed from open without carrying position, so archive-then-live equals the original only when every closed row precedes every open one, and the fixture is built exactly that way; the comment stating it as a general property is a false sentence. Closing S14 while S13 stays open rebuilds S12 S14 S13 S15 S16 against an original S12 S13 S14 S15 S16, which is what the next sitting does to S13 through S16. Also: packet.mjs takes --root only after the command word, and nothing pins the new gate step, since kitCheck rule G asks only that some step name each tool. Correction 1 issued, and at sweep tier it is the only one. What both reviewers confirmed: coverage did not drop, checkErrors is byte-identical across the split, and the two steps fail independently in both directions. The separate process is the review of record; the in-session agent reaches the owner only through the party that wrote the envelope, which is weaker independence than a review of that envelope deserves.

Seven ledger rows written this session were plain strings where the schema is {at, event}, so renderBoard printed each as 'function at() { [native code] } undefined' and the whole session's record was invisible on the generated board. Repaired in place at 0295f0b. No check parses a ledger row, which is why twenty green gate steps said nothing: T59's shape exactly, packages.json shipped broken and unread for three landings and board.ledger has now done the same. The archive escaped because rotate had only moved well-formed rows; rotate derives the archive filename from rows[0].at, so one more rotation would have written a file named after a native function. The spark this deserves waits until rotate clears sparks.json, because AGENTS section 4 forbids appending to a live file that is over budget.

F33 correction 1 reviewed at 156f40b: CORRECTIONS NEEDED again, and the correction cap is spent, so the lane splits off this seat. All five items do go red on revert, coverage did not regress and the rebase is proven, but rotate's `at` is an index into the list as it stood at that rotation, so a second productive rotation collides: archiving the live store, absorbing S14, rotating again writes S14 at slot 1 against S02 at slot 1, duplicate slots {1: 2}, and the reconstruction the comment and the archive header both promise is impossible. The control plane's own verification missed it by driving one rotation where the reviewer drove two. The same disease appears in item 2, where the --root order assertion passes even when the flag's value is ignored, because the fixture and the live tree both print packet check ok. Both are the original defect's shape: a property true only in the degenerate case. The issuance is at fault too — the correction envelope offered a choice between carrying position and narrowing the claim, and a sweep-tier envelope should not hand a cheap seat that judgement. The split envelope dictates the narrow claim instead of offering it.

F33 split to a fresh seat at base 805be61, same cheap tier, with an envelope that dictates rather than offers. Six items, mostly deletion: rotate stops writing `at` and nothing promises the archive can rebuild the live file, because position indexes the list as it stood at that rotation and collides on the second; the comment and archive header say what is true, that rotation is not a reversible transform; four replacement assertions each with a named mutation that makes them fail, including the two-productive-rotations case both prior passes skipped; the --root fixture becomes over-cap so a flag whose value is ignored cannot pass green; a non-number cap takes the missing-cap path; and two false sentences leave the lane log. The issuance lesson is recorded in the envelope itself: a sweep-tier envelope that offers a cheap seat a choice between a hard correct option and an easy correct one will get the hard one done wrong, which is how both of this lane's defects entered.

F33 landed from writer/F33 at 8da5e53, fast-forward, after one correction and a split to a fresh seat on the same cheap tier. What it built: the reading-path gate step is two steps, so a suspension can be narrower than its hypothesis and F31's prefix guard survives one that targets the budget, which is what X01 got wrong; sizeBudget prints a percentage of cap for every budgeted file and the three context budgets and bands at 80, implementing the rule AGENTS section 4 has carried since F0 with nothing enforcing it; and spark.mjs rotate windows the store as ledger.mjs windows the ledger. Measured at landing: node factory/tools/spark.mjs rotate printed moved 12 kept 4, factory/sparks.json went 8332 to 2457 bytes, and node factory/tools/packet.mjs cost puts the control-plane packet at 36.3 KB against a 44 KB cap, down from 42.1. Three independent reviews ran, two of them separate claude -p processes; each of the first two found a blocking defect the control plane's own verification had missed, both of the same shape, an assertion satisfied by construction. docs/sparks/*.md now carries a 48 KB glob cap, which the lane named and could not add.

F34 landed as a control-plane records commit, not a writer envelope. AGENTS section 8 has the control plane write documentation directly, section 3 gives a records envelope no review, and T53 makes an archive-at-80-per-cent cut a records commit that does not issue a writer. A voluntary review ran anyway, because the commit edits the constitution, and it found the blocking defect described below. Three changes. AGENTS section 3 carries D-53's orchestration model: order follows the dependency the board states rather than the issuer's judgement, siblings run only on holds proved disjoint at the files and written down with a free slot not counting as proof, review slots are reserved so a returned lane never waits, and a seat census is read from the process table with a dead seat resumed on its own session id. The provisional group of D-49 moved to factory/OPERATING_MODEL.md under a table naming what enforces each bullet, checked at the objects: eight of the nine rows name a trap in the digest every packet carries, and the ninth, a writer never fast-forwards main, is already AGENTS section 3's push the branch only, never main. A duplicate moved, not a law. Section 9's index kept the rows a seat or an issuing control plane reaches for constantly and the rest moved verbatim, thirty-seven rows byte-identical. The review caught the control plane writing a rule with no object into the file every seat reads: the first draft said a lane carries a wave and a depends-on and order is derived from that graph, while no lane carries either field, nothing renders them and nothing checks them. That is D-54's own charge, a rule with no check is a diary, committed into the constitution by the session that had just read D-54. The sentence now states what the board supports and names F37 as the lane that would derive order from a field. It also caught One review slot as a threshold no dated row carries, against AGENTS section 6, and three numbers in this row that did not reproduce, which is why the sizes here are a command rather than digits: node factory/tools/sizeBudget.mjs prints AGENTS.md at 86.6 per cent of its 12 KB cap against 96.8 before, and the control-plane packet out of the band. The seat-packet and control-plane figures move when this row is written, so they are not pasted here (T04). factory/COPY.md pointed a child at a part of section 5 that moved and was corrected. factory/OPERATING_MODEL.md gained a 16 KB cap: a file that receives what a capped file sheds while being unmeasured itself is T01.

seatPacketKb returned to 26 by D-57, and F36 narrowed by D-58, both before F36 was issued rather than after it failed. D-56 raised the cap to 27 under protest and named the condition for the pressure coming off, F36 bringing the packet under 26; F34 did it by another route, so node factory/tools/packet.mjs cost now prints the seat packet at 25.3 KB and the band prints 97.4 per cent of 26. Leaving the cap at 27 would have kept a concession whose reason had expired. F36's method also collided with F31: a per-lane traps digest makes the bytes before the envelope differ by lane, which is the assertion X01 was reverted for nearly switching off, and it would silently retire the proof F34 rested on, that every provisional bullet is enforced by a trap in the digest every packet carries. So F36 keeps the half that is safe and still changes the slope, a trap naming its object plus compressing the traps that already name a check, and per-lane scoping is deferred with a trigger rather than dropped: the seat packet reaching 90 per cent again with no duplicate left to shed.

F36 issued at base 2c1159c, alone, narrowed by D-58. Three things: every trap gains an object naming the file or glob it binds to or a star meaning it binds everywhere; packet.mjs --self-test asserts every trap has one and that every non-star object resolves in the tree, so a trap pointing at a file that is not there fails the gate; and trapsDigest emits only the first sentence of a trap that already names a check, which is D-52's second remedy at about 2.7 KB and makes writing a check remove a trap's prose from every future packet. The envelope names what is NOT in scope and why, because the board's title still promises the deferred half. Envelope is 5877 bytes against a 6144 cap.

F36 returned at 5c8f2ce and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED, on the same defect for the third time in two lanes: an assertion satisfied by construction. The compression claim built its expected line by calling firstSentence and ruleNamesACheck, the same two functions trapsDigest calls to build the line being compared, so it pinned a ternary and nothing else; the reviewer gutted compression twice with one-line mutations and the gate stayed green, once turning compression off entirely at 12261 bytes and once truncating all seventy-one rows to 6923. The object-resolves claim had no vacuity guard where its sibling did, so setting every object to star made it vanish silently. The lane's substance is good and confirmed at the objects: 71 objects with 19 non-star all resolving and 52 star rows judged honest against their rule text, no stored rule edited, no digest row dropped, and F31's prefix byte-identical across two lanes with the envelope still last, which is what D-58 deferred the scoping half to protect. Correction 1 issued, narrower than the first envelope: traps.yaml is finished and withheld, and the correction may not write an assertion in terms of the functions that produce what it asserts.

F36 landed from writer/F36 at b106bd2, fast-forward, after one correction. Every trap carries an object: 52 are a star meaning it binds everywhere, 19 name a path, and node factory/tools/packet.mjs --self-test fails when a trap has no object, when a non-star object does not resolve in the tree, and when no trap carries a non-star object at all. trapsDigest emits only the first sentence of a trap whose stored rule names a check, and the stored rule keeps every sentence it had: traps.yaml took 71 insertions and 0 deletions. Measured at the objects: seat packet 25.3 to 23.6 KB, 90.9 per cent of the 26 KB cap D-57 restored, and the traps digest 12.0 to 10.3 KB. Digest to digest the compression removed 1702 bytes against D-52's estimate of about 2.7 KB, and the lane log carries both rather than adopting the estimate. F31 survives untouched, which is what D-58 deferred the scoping half to protect: the envelope part is last and the bytes before it are byte-identical for two different lanes, checked directly rather than through the self-test that claims it.
